name: Automotive & Electric Vehicles
one_liner: Vehicle manufacturers and their suppliers, a capital-intensive, cyclical industry being reshaped by electrification, software, and shifting trade policy.
how_it_makes_money: Automakers sell vehicles through franchised dealers (or directly, in the case of Tesla and some EV startups), earning margin on each unit plus captive financing income. Parts and service, software, and regulatory credits are additional revenue streams.
revenue_formula: Revenue = units sold × average transaction price (ATP) − incentives
Profit = units × (ATP − variable cost per unit) − fixed costs
Lifetime revenue = vehicle sale + financing + parts and service + software subscriptions
cost_structure: Materials and components: the dominant cost, with batteries a large share of EV cost
Capital expenditure for plants and tooling
margins: Traditional automakers typically earn mid-single-digit operating margins, with trucks and SUVs far more profitable than small cars. Many EV programs remain less profitable than gas equivalents due to battery costs, while scale, product mix, and pricing discipline drive differences.

key_metrics.name: Units sold / deliveries
key_metrics.what: Volume of vehicles sold, the primary scale metric.

key_metrics.name: Average transaction price (ATP)
key_metrics.what: Average price paid, reflecting mix and pricing power.

key_metrics.name: Incentive spend per unit
key_metrics.what: Discounts needed to move vehicles, a sign of demand strength.

key_metrics.name: Days supply of inventory
key_metrics.what: How many days of sales dealers hold, signaling demand-supply balance.

key_metrics.name: Battery cost per kWh
key_metrics.what: Key driver of EV cost competitiveness.

key_metrics.name: Capacity utilization
key_metrics.what: How fully plants are used, driving fixed-cost absorption.

trends: EV adoption slower than expected in the US, with automakers scaling back targets and pivoting to hybrids
Chinese automakers such as BYD gaining global share with low-cost EVs
Tariffs and trade policy reshaping supply chains and plant locations
Software-defined vehicles and driver assistance as future revenue sources
Battery supply chain localization and new chemistries
Robotaxi and autonomous driving commercialization efforts
